To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

recycling is an effective strategy to reduce emissions for all common materials except glass, that recycling decisions should be coordinated across the supply chain, and that a social planner could implement a deposit/refund policy to achieve this objective.

recycling of common materials is effective in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and aggregate costs; that a product manufacturer or a private recycling firm may be the best choice to run a recycling operation, depending on material and market characteristics; and that a deposit/refound scheme may lead to the optimal collection rates, if the social planner refunds the money to local governments.

(a) Recycling is effective in terms of emissions, operational costs and social costs for paper, plastics, and metals, and it is not effective for glass; (b) In some scenarios, a manufacturer or an independent recycler might be the best candidate for organizing recycling operations; and (c) A deposit/refund scheme might lead to a social optimal collection rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effectiveness of recycling, optimal decisions for recyclers, and coordination mechanisms to bring recycling decisions closer to social optimum.
a number of questions about the effectiveness, optimal decisions, coordination mechanisms, and incentives in common material recycling.

the effectiveness of recycling common materials in reducing emissions, and with the design of recycling operations, including optimal decisions, and incentives that can be offered to local governments, product manufacturers, and independent firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
recycling is effective and should be implemented, and that it is not necessarily the case that the local government is the best choice to manage the recycling process.

recycling is a viable option to reduce emissions, and that recycling operations should be organized by the entity that is best suited to manage the trade-offs among the three dimensions we considered.

the effectiveness of recycling is material-dependent, that the optimal recycling decision is material- and decision-maker-dependent, and that the optimal recycling incentives are also material- and decision maker-dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the effectiveness of recycling depends on material-specific properties.
recycling is effective and that there are instances when a product manufacturer or independent recyclers can be the best choice in organizing recycling operations.

, in general, recycling is an effective way to reduce emissions and costs, but the choice of who should be in charge of organizing recycling operations should be based on a case-by-case basis, and the incentives to be used by a social planner should be based on the specific characteristics of a material and a supply chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social planner should be able to use a deposit/refund system as a coordination mechanism to achieve a socially optimal outcome.
recycling common materials is an effective way to reduce emissions and aggregate costs.
recycling is a cost-effective way of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and that it is also cost-effective with respect to operational costs.
